title: The RDW–MCV product adds no clear HbA1c prediction benefit beyond flexible routine measures across two NHANES cycles
abstract: We tested whether RDW-CV times mean corpuscular volume, a proxy for absolute erythrocyte volume spread, predicts measured HbA1c beyond fasting plasma glucose and flexible additive routine indices. A frozen weighted spline model was trained in 2,342 NHANES 2013–2014 adults and evaluated without refitting in 2,211 separately sampled 2015–2016 adults. Adding the product changed weighted mean squared error from 0.249048 to 0.248901 squared HbA1c percentage points (difference −0.000147). The paired rescaled-PSU-bootstrap 95% interval was −0.000507 to +0.000183; refitting both cycles with fixed preprocessing knots gave −0.000624 to +0.001276. Discovery-cycle grouped cross-validation worsened slightly. The apparent improvement was larger with a linear baseline and shrank with nonlinear adjustment. These data do not establish useful incremental information from the product, red-cell lifespan inference, improved glycemia measurement or clinical benefit.
